q: How do I report Scope 2 when my factory buys solar power through a group captive or open access arrangement?
title: Reporting group captive solar in Scope 2
short: Report both ways. Location-based Scope 2 applies the grid factor to all the electricity you consume, including the wheeled solar. Market-based Scope 2 can treat the solar units adjusted on your bill as zero, if your contract gives you their renewable attributes and nobody sold RECs for them.
audience: Factories in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka using group captive or open access solar

sections.h: Why location-based Scope 2 does not fall
p: Wheeled solar travels over the same grid as everyone else's power. The GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance defines location-based Scope 2 as the average intensity of the grid where you consume, so it is total consumption times the grid factor, whatever you contracted. Only a direct private line from a plant to your factory, with no grid in between, changes that.

sections.h: When the solar can count as zero in market-based
p: The guidance sets quality criteria for contractual instruments. For a group captive or open access deal, check each one:
ul: The contract conveys the renewable attributes of the generation to you.
Only you claim them: no RECs issued and sold for the same MWh, and the generator does not claim them elsewhere.
The units are from the reporting period, or close to it.
The plant is in the same market as your load. Plants on India's national grid are generally treated as one market.
Claim the units adjusted at your meter on the discom bill, after transmission and wheeling losses, not the units the plant injected.
Banked units are claimed when they are adjusted against your consumption; note their generation months, since the guidance asks for instruments as close as possible to the period of use.
Lapsed banked units that were never adjusted against your load cannot be claimed.

sections.h: What to use for the remaining grid power
p: India does not publish a residual mix factor. Use the CEA grid average for the units still drawn from the grid, and say in your report that it is a proxy for the residual mix. This slightly understates market-based Scope 2, because the grid average still contains renewables that others have claimed.

ol: The power purchase or shareholder agreement clause on renewable attributes.
Monthly discom bills showing units adjusted.
The energy account from the state load despatch centre or the generator.
A declaration from the generator that no RECs were issued or sold for your units.

p: Principle 6, Essential Indicator 1 of the BRSR format asks for energy in joules or multiples, split by source. Enter the solar units adjusted at your meter as renewable and the rest as non-renewable, converting at 3.6 GJ per MWh:
ul: From renewable sources, total electricity consumption (A): the adjusted group captive or open access units.
From non-renewable sources, total electricity consumption (D): the units still drawn from the discom grid.

Essential Indicator 7, total Scope 2 emissions in metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent: BRSR names no method, so say in a note whether the figure is location-based or market-based, and keep the same choice every year.

sections.h: A method note you can adapt
p: "Scope 2 is reported on both bases. Location-based applies the CEA CO2 Baseline Database [version] weighted average for [financial year], [factor] t CO2 per MWh, to all electricity consumed. Market-based counts [X] MWh of solar, adjusted at our meter under a [group captive / open access] agreement that assigns the renewable attributes to us, as zero, and applies the same CEA average to the remaining [Y] MWh as a proxy, because India publishes no residual mix factor. No RECs or carbon credits were sold for the claimed units."

example.title: Worked example: one year with group captive solar
lines: Total consumption: 1,000 MWh, of which 600 MWh adjusted as group captive solar
Location-based: 1,000 MWh x 0.710 t CO2 per MWh for FY 2024-25 = 710 t CO2
Market-based: solar 600 MWh at zero; grid 400 MWh x 0.710 = 284 t CO2
Report both: 710 t CO2 location-based and 284 t CO2 market-based, with the residual mix proxy disclosed
BRSR energy table: renewable 600 x 3.6 = 2,160 GJ; non-renewable 400 x 3.6 = 1,440 GJ; renewable share 60 percent
example.note: The 284 t figure holds only if the solar attributes are contractually yours and not sold as RECs.

senseible: Senseible reports location-based Scope 2 from the kWh on your electricity bills at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, and market-based Scope 2 when you supply the contract or certificate data. It does not verify that the attribute claim is valid.
